name: kill-switch
context: Deployed agents need an out-of-band control plane to halt, pause, or drain running instances without redeploying code.
use_cases: Halt agent fleet during an incident
Emergency stop for a coding agent
Isolate a specific tenant's agent without affecting others
Enter read-only degraded mode (block write actions while allowing reads)
avoid_when: No on-call process exists to operate it
Fully automated environments where human intervention is unavailable
anti_patterns: No authorization on the switch itself
In-band stop hook that relies on agent checking it voluntarily
Kill state cached for minutes instead of seconds (renders switch useless in emergencies)
design_principles: The switch must be independent of the agent runtime
Kill switch must be enforced by runtime, not model volition
In-flight actions must complete or rollback; kill switch blocks new actions only
best_practices: Conduct scheduled kill drills in staging at least quarterly
Verify kill propagation completes within target latency (≤5 seconds)
references: Agent Patterns Catalog, Kill Switch pattern — https://www.agentpatternscatalog.org/patterns/kill-switch/
